title: Assistance for School Canteen Vendors to Offset Rising Costs
what_it_is: Assistance for School Canteen Vendors to Offset Rising Costs

sections.label: MOE monitors school canteen food
sections.summary: MOE works with schools to monitor canteen food quality, quantity and prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) works with schools to monitor canteen food quality, quantity and prices.

sections.label: Stallholder monthly rentals
sections.summary: Individual stallholders are charged rentals of between $5 and $15 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Individual stallholders are charged rentals of between $5 and $15 per month.

sections.label: Meal subsidies for FAS students
sections.summary: Students from lower-income families on MOE's Financial Assistance Scheme receive school meal subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Students from lower-income families on MOE’s Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS) receive school meal subsidies.

sections.label: Central kitchen meal pilot
sections.summary: Meals can be pre-ordered and prepared at a central kitchen before delivery to schools, piloted at Yusof Ishak Secondary School and shown effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: For example, meals can be pre-ordered and prepared at a central kitchen before they are delivered to schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: This model has been piloted at Yusof Ishak Secondary School and shown to be effective.

sections.label: Vending machines for drinks
sections.summary: Most vending machines are for drinks, reducing manpower needed to serve them and freeing manpower for hot meals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Most of the vending machines are for drinks so that we can reduce the manpower required to serve them in our canteens and we can have the rest of the manpower available to have hot meals for our students.

sections.label: Local farm ingredient collaborations
sections.summary: The Ministry was asked if it explored collaborations with local farms or producers to supply fresh, nutritious ingredients at reduced cost to canteens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And second, in view of the rising ingredient costs, has the Ministry explored collaborations with local farms or producers to supply fresh, nutritious ingredients at a reduced cost to school canteens?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: We will try what we can to help our stallholders to get the most cost-effective produce for their stalls.

sections.label: Suitable cost-effective school produce
sections.summary: The primary concern is that produce acquired and purchased is suitable for the school and vendors and is cost-effective.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Our primary concern is to make sure that the produce acquired, purchased, is suitable for the school, for the vendors, and also that it is cost-effective.

sections.label: Learning civic responsibility from Japanese
sections.summary: This differs from existing models, and in civic responsibility much can be learned from the Japanese in how children care for their school environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, this is quite different from the models that we have.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Certainly, in terms of civic responsibility, we can learn much from the Japanese in how the children come together to take care of their school environment, including keeping their classrooms clean, even though they consume food within their classrooms.
